items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: That's the band that had Jimmy, I mean, Benny Goodman. And Glenn Miller was making the arrangements... I got home on a vacation when I was with Ben Pollack's band.

ctx.x: So you, well, you'd come back for a visit though, on vacation or something.

I came back, I came back in 1940. No, I didn't, I didn't get back until 1940. I think I, I, I, I went to, I think it was my dad's funeral or my mother's. I can't remember which one, 1940. Because I was in the Army when, when the other, one of the, one of the other died and I was out of Vallejo, California at that time. But anyway, but the, the only time I, I got home, I, I, I got home on a vacation when I was with Ben Pollack's band. I don't remember now. We were playing at the Florentine Grill Room at the Park…

Yeah, I, I, I thought maybe you'd come back when you were pretty rich. I read something about a show that Charles Dillingham had. Do you know that name? Dillingham. Yeah, Charles Dillingham had a show. Where? In New York. This was in the, this was in the, in the local, you know, uh, 174 magazine. The Union magazine, yeah.

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: listen to Barney B. God playing and all

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Yeah. So. Well, you, you were telling me yesterday about the 100 block of North Rampart, how you couldn't get in that place where Zooty was. I didn't get in there.

Yeah. I told you that. Yeah. I told you, my brother, my brother brought me in the front and he says, take off your hat here. He says, cause there's the best of the best in that place. Mm-hmm. And he says, I'm going in there, have a band, I'll have Zooty open that window around in the back alley. Mm-hmm. There's an alley in the back of all those places. Mm-hmm. So, Zooty did that and, and, and that, that's what happened. Because I had long pants on at that time, cause I used to go and dance on the boat with these…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: we had to take the Benny Goodman. Yeah. Sing.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's, but anyway, she was with the Bob Crosby band.

Yeah, she, she stayed with the Bob, she sang on the Fitch bandwagon with us. Mm-hmm. And, and that's when we did the Camel Show and then, and a lot of politics went along and we had to take the Benny Goodman. Yeah. Sing. All these, these are, these are pictures, just copies. Mm-hmm. This is one of the greatest pictures. We went to the Apollo Theater in New York to see Louie Armstrong. He was playing at the County's Inn. Mm-hmm. And we went backstage to see him. This friend, uh, Hal Peterson, uh, not Hal, uh,…
He played banjo with him, see.
